ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give prompt notice of the claim, Vendor shall control the defence, and Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation at Vendor's expense. If the Services or a Deliverable are alleged to infringe, Vendor shall at its expense procure the right to continue use, modify or replace the affected item so it is non-infringing, or refund Fees paid for it.

input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement references indemnity remedies (Sections 9.3 and 20.5) but contains no indemnification section, so we have inserted a Vendor indemnity covering third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and wilful misconduct, with standard procedure and IP remedies. Our position is that Vendor indemnifies for these risks and that indemnities sit outside the liability cap (Section 21.3).
input.summary: Insert Vendor indemnity (IP, law, data breach, wilful misconduct) after Section 21.4.

input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we may develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the non-compete; it is also inconsistent with Section 12.3. If Vendor needs protection we can discuss a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
input.summary: Delete the 24-month, any-territory non-compete on Customer.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: Neither Party shall solicit for employment any personnel of the other Party who are directly involved in performing or receiving the Services, for twelve months after the end of that person's involvement. This does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at the other Party's personnel, or the hiring of any person who responds to them or approaches a Party unsolicited.

input.comment: [Playbook] We have narrowed the restriction to our fallback: mutual, limited to personnel involved in the Services, twelve months, with a general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-out, and no no-hire element. A 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees is not something we can accept.
input.summary: Narrow the no-hire to a mutual 12-month non-solicit with carve-outs.

input.comment: [Playbook] We do not give most-favoured-nation or match-and-disclose rights to suppliers, so we have deleted this obligation; MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome. Section 12.3 already confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment has been made.
input.summary: Delete Customer's obligation to disclose and match third-party offers.
